user_requirements: This is a VERIFICATION-AND-HARDENING review, not a fresh analysis. The corpus contains REPORT.md — ASG Security's LCF Pilot Accountability & Value Report to Heart of the City (funder: Local Crime Fund, Auckland Council money; audience: Edward Caughey and the joint funding administrators) — together with its complete underlying source data: final_stats.txt (canonical statistics), daily_data.csv (48 verified days), weekly_reports_totals.txt (the weekly data reports the totals must reconcile with), baseline_and_yoy.txt (pre-pilot baseline and 2025 comparison data), and lcf_contract_facts.txt (funding agreement facts and constraints). Your job: (1) verify EVERY number, percentage and date in REPORT.md against the source files — recompute the derived figures (weekly averages, +45% vs baseline, +28% vs last year, -12% police YoY, per-day rates) and flag any that do not reproduce; (2) check internal consistency — totals vs weekly tables vs narrative claims; (3) flag any claim not supported by the corpus, any accidental survey-results claim (none may be cited), any breach of the required CPTED framing or the no-tender-language constraint, and anything an experienced Council funding administrator would challenge; (4) assess tone for a funder accountability audience — confident but not promotional; (5) list concrete corrections. Output a findings report with severity ratings (CRITICAL / MAJOR / MINOR / PASS), the exact current text, and the exact corrected text for each finding. Do not rewrite the report wholesale — produce the findings list.
acquirer_context: ASG Security (Absolute Security Group Ltd) reports to Heart of the City as funding holder; HOTC reports onward to the joint LCF funding administrators at Auckland Council by 31 July 2026. The report must withstand line-by-line scrutiny by a Council community-safety advisor. A previous ASG document was queried by HOTC for one mis-attributed statistic, so unsupported attribution is the highest-risk defect class.
